decisions.reason: Share Kanazawa is a GOI-designed welfare and mixed-community project; Kanazawa Bunka Hall is a different cultural venue that only shares the city name.
Tama Art University Library and Musashino Art University Library belong to different universities, years and architects.
Inujima Seirensho Art Museum is an industrial-site museum on Inujima; Musashino Art University Library is an unrelated Tokyo university building.
Teshima Art Museum and Musashino Art University Library merely share a 2010 completion year; project, island location and architect differ.
Hoki Museum is a 2010 Nikken Sekkei museum in Chiba; Miho Museum is a 1997 I. M. Pei project in Shiga.

Oita Prefectural Art Museum and Aspen Art Museum only share architect and completion year; project name, city, country and program identity differ. Architect normalization now routes the Oita case directly to new-building-candidate instead of a misleading prefectural-museum match.
Nagasaki and Yamanashi prefectural art museums are separate institutions in different prefectures with different architects.
Sagawa Art Museum and Iwasaki Art Museum are different institutions, cities and completion years.
Fukuda Art Museum in Kyoto opened in 2019; Fukuoka Art Museum is a separate 1979 institution in Fukuoka.
Tonami Public Library is a 2020 Japanese municipal library; the New York performing-arts library is unrelated in geography, program and year.
Ishikawa Prefectural Library is a 2022 library; Kagawa Prefectural Government Office is a 1958 government building in another prefecture.
Helsinki Central Library Oodi and Central Library, Des Moines are separate libraries in different countries, years and architects.
Kunsthaus Graz is a 2003 Peter Cook and Colin Fournier project; Kunsthal Rotterdam is a 1992 OMA project.
LocHal is a 2019 Tilburg railway-workshop conversion; Schocken Library is an unrelated historic library separated by 84 years.
Markthal Rotterdam is a 2014 MVRDV market-housing complex; Kunsthal Rotterdam is a 1992 OMA exhibition building.
Oslo Opera House and Guangzhou Opera House are separate projects in different countries, years and architects.
Harpa in Reykjavik and Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles are separate concert halls with different architects and completion years.
